mainTopic: חמר גמל, stepping outside the תחום, and the end of פרק מי שהוציאוהו
overview: The amud opens by asking whose view the story of רב נתן בר אושעיא follows, and concludes that it could fit either רב יוסף or רבה. Next, the גמרא asks why our משנה repeats רבי מאיר's ruling of חמר גמל. רב ששת answers that the earlier משנה covered only a doubtful עירוב, while ours teaches that he is a חמר גמל even when he certainly made no עירוב. A new משנה then rules that someone who stepped outside his תחום may not come back in, while רבי אליעזר allows it from two אמות. The גמרא brings two versions of רבי חנינא about a person with one foot in and one foot out, linking the lenient view to אחרים, who go by where most of the body is. It then reconciles conflicting ברייתות about רבי אליעזר's numbers, explaining one as counting differently and the other as speaking of a מודד. Another משנה rules that a traveler caught outside the תחום at nightfall may not enter, but רבי שמעון allows fifteen אמות because surveyors set the marker inside the true limit to guard against measuring errors. The פרק ends, and the next פרק begins explaining how a city's border is drawn, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Whose view did רב נתן בר אושעיא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the story of רב נתן בר אושעיא fits רב יוסף's explanation, following רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow? Is it רב יוסף's explanation, following רבי יוסי בר יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the story just told and asks which opinion it matches. It proposes one answer: רב יוסף's explanation, following רבי יוסי בר יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבה and רב יוסף disagreed about what exactly רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי בר יהודה argue over: whether the person must have set out on his way, and whether he must say out loud where his שבת home is. In the story, nobody is described as making a spoken declaration. So the גמרא first thinks this fits רב יוסף, who says everyone requires setting out, combined with רבי יוסי בר יהודה, who says no declaration is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Which opinion does this follow?
According to the view of
A person's official שבת resting place, from which his limits are measured

phrases.english: Like whom (does this follow)?
phrases.notes: Refers to the story of רב נתן בר אושעיא just told

phrases.english: Like Rav Yosef,
phrases.notes: Who said everyone agrees that one must have set out on the way

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda?
phrases.notes: Who holds that no spoken declaration is needed

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן — כְּרַב יוֹסֵף, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by linking the preceding story to the earlier dispute between רבה and רב יוסף
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which explanation and which תנא the conduct of רב נתן בר אושעיא follows
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Suggested: רב יוסף, following רבי יוסי בר יהודה

steps.title: It could also follow רבה and רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. The story could also fit רבה's explanation, following רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It could follow רבה, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the story does not prove the first suggestion. It can also be explained according to רבה, following רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on assuming no declaration was made. But we can say that רב יהודה בר אשתתא did declare his resting place, even though the story does not mention it. If so, the story also fits רבי יהודה, who requires a declaration, as רבה explains him. The story therefore cannot decide between the two views.

keyTerms.meaning: No. Introduces a rejection of the previous suggestion

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling that the הלכה follows רבה. The גמרא only shows that the story can fit him too, so it proves nothing either way.

phrases.english: No, (it is) like Rabba,
phrases.notes: Rejects the claim that the story must follow רב יוסף

phrases.english: and according to Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: Assume a declaration of the resting place was made, as רבי יהודה requires

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the identification proposed in step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that the story proves רב יוסף's view. It does not reject רב יוסף's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed no declaration was made. A declaration may have been made without being reported.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a common pattern: a story counts as proof only if it cannot be explained any other way.

steps.title: Quoting רבי מאיר in our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר's statement in our משנה: whoever could have made an עירוב and did not is a חמר גמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: anyone who is able to make an עירוב, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting a line from our משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case is a person who left his home to place an עירוב, which gave up his original resting place, and then did not finish making it. רבי מאיר says such a person is a חמר גמל, meaning he is restricted on both sides. The גמרא is about to ask why this line is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: To make an עירוב (here an עירוב תחומין, which sets a new Shabbos home base)
Etc. Signals that the quote from the משנה continues

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
phrases.notes: Quoting our משנה

phrases.english: Anyone who is able to make an eiruv, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: and did not make it, he is a חמר גמל

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר כֹּל שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְעָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion on another line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, one who could have made an עירוב and did not is a חמר גמל

steps.title: Didn't we already learn this in another משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges our משנה as repetitive. An earlier משנה already teaches that רבי מאיר holds a doubtful case is חמר גמל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we already learned this once before: in a case of doubt, רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה say this person is a חמר גמל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי מאיר's ruling needs to appear here, since another משנה already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier משנה dealt with a doubtful עירוב, where we are unsure whether it was valid. There רבי מאיר already ruled that the person is a חמר גמל. Since a משנה should not repeat itself for no reason, the גמרא asks what new point our משנה adds.

keyTerms.meaning: But we already learned. A standard challenge that something is repetitive
One time (before)
A doubtful case
A donkey driver and a camel driver at once: pulled two ways, so he may walk only where both sets of Shabbos limits overlap

steps.confusionAlert: חמר גמל does not mean he cannot move at all. He gets only the overlap of two areas, the limits from his original home and the limits from his intended עירוב spot, so he ends up with less than either.

phrases.english: But we already learned it once:
phrases.notes: Refers to an earlier משנה in this tractate

phrases.aramaic: סָפֵק, רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: (In a case of) doubt, Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda say:
phrases.notes: Doubt about whether the עירוב was valid

phrases.english: This person is a donkey driver and camel driver.
phrases.notes: Restricted on both sides

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the line quoted in step 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for רבי מאיר's ruling in our משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier משנה already has רבי מאיר ruling חמר גמל in a doubtful case, so repeating it here seems unnecessary

steps.title: Even when he certainly made no עירוב, he is a חמר גמל
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that our משנה adds something new. Even when it is certain that no עירוב was made, רבי מאיר still rules חמר גמל, not just in a doubtful case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Do not say that רבי מאיר's reason applies only when there is doubt whether he made an עירוב, so that only then is he a חמר גמל, but when he certainly did not make an עירוב he is not a חמר גמל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge. He shows that the two משניות teach different cases: the earlier one covers doubt, and ours covers certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the earlier משנה alone, we might think the double restriction comes only from the doubt: maybe the עירוב worked and maybe it didn't, so we are strict both ways. Then if he certainly made no עירוב, we would say he simply keeps his original home's limits. Our משנה teaches that even with certainty he is a חמר גמל, because leaving to make the עירוב already gave up his original resting place.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say. Introduces a mistaken assumption that the משנה comes to block
The reason
Certainly, for sure (the opposite of סָפֵק)
He made an עירוב

steps.whatToRemember: The earlier משנה teaches חמר גמל in a doubtful case. Our משנה teaches חמר גמל even when it is certain that no עירוב was made. So the two משניות are not repetitive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that for רבי מאיר, the double restriction comes from giving up the original home, not only from doubt. That shapes how we understand the whole rule of חמר גמל.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
phrases.notes: Answering the challenge of step 4

phrases.english: Do not say that the reason of Rabbi Meir
phrases.notes: Introduces the mistake our משנה prevents

phrases.english: (is only when it is) doubtful whether he made an eiruv or did not,
phrases.notes: The case of the earlier משנה

phrases.english: that he is a donkey driver and camel driver,
but (when) he certainly did not make an eiruv,
phrases.notes: The case of our משנה

phrases.english: he is not a donkey driver and camel driver.
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken idea our משנה comes to reject

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לָא תֵּימָא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by separating the doubtful case from the certain case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: the earlier משנה covers doubt, our משנה covers certainty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think רבי מאיר imposes חמר גמל only because of doubt, so with certainty the person would keep his original home's limits
steps.terutzMaskana: Even when he certainly made no עירוב, he is a חמר גמל according to רבי מאיר

steps.title: Even a certain lack of עירוב can lead to חמר גמל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רב ששת's answer. רבי מאיר's ruling of חמר גמל applies even when it is certain that no עירוב was made, as in our case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even when he certainly did not make an עירוב, he can be a חמר גמל. Here he certainly did not make an עירוב, and still he is a חמר גמל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up רב ששת's answer. It explains exactly what new point our משנה adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה only taught חמר גמל in a doubtful case, where we don't know if the עירוב worked. Our משנה adds a case where it is certain that no עירוב was made. The person is still stuck as a חמר גמל, because his doubt is about which place counts as his home. So our משנה is not repetitive.

keyTerms.meaning: Certain, definite
A שבת arrangement (here, an עירוב תחומין) / he made one
A donkey driver and camel driver. This describes someone stuck between two directions, who may only walk where both possible positions allow.

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה adds that חמר גמל can apply even when it is certain that no עירוב was made, not only when we are unsure whether the עירוב worked.

phrases.english: Rather: even when he certainly did not make an eiruv
he can be a donkey-driver camel-driver.
For here he certainly did not make an eiruv,
and yet he is a donkey-driver camel-driver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ששת's answer from Step 5 and closes the question of why our משנה is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה is not repetitive. It teaches חמר גמל even when it is certain that no עירוב was made.

steps.title: New משנה: someone who went outside his תחום
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that someone who left his תחום by even one אמה may not come back in. רבי אליעזר allows coming back after two אמות, but not after three.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person who went outside the תחום, even by one אמה, may not come back in. רבי אליעזר says: two אמות, he may come back in; three, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a person who stepped beyond his 2,000-אמה שבת boundary and asks whether he may come back inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once he is outside the תחום, he is limited to the small area around where he stands. So the question is whether he may return to his original area. The תנא קמא forbids it for even one אמה. רבי אליעזר is more lenient for a very small distance (two אמות) but not for three.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
The שבת boundary, 2,000 אמות from where one is based
A cubit, a unit of length
He may enter, come back in

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two numbers. רבי אליעזר permits two אמות and forbids three. The תנא קמא forbids even one.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who went out beyond the Shabbat limit,
even one cubit, may not reenter.
Rabbi Eliezer says:
Two cubits, he may reenter;
three, he may not reenter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the חמר גמל discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going out even one אמה beyond the תחום means he may not come back in (תנא קמא). רבי אליעזר permits coming back from two אמות but not from three.

steps.title: One foot outside is enough to forbid coming back in
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules that if one foot is inside the תחום and one foot is outside, he may not come back in. He learns this from the spelling of רגלך in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חנינא said: If one foot is inside the תחום and one foot is outside, he may not come back in. As it says, 'If you turn away your foot because of שבת.' The word is spelled 'your foot' (singular).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי חנינא's ruling about a person standing with one foot on each side of the line. He even gives a source from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רגלך in ישעיה is written without a yud, so it can be read as 'your foot' (one foot). This shows that one foot alone matters for שבת. So one foot outside counts as being outside, and he may not come back in.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Your foot. Here it is written in a way that reads as singular.
It is written (the spelling, as opposed to how it is read)

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is from how the word is spelled, not how it is pronounced. The written form (without a yud) reads as one foot.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Ḥanina said:
If one of his feet is within the limit,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַגְלוֹ אַחַת חוּץ לַתְּחוּם — לֹא יִכָּנֵס,
phrases.english: and his other foot is beyond the limit, he may not reenter,
as it is written: “If you turn away your feet because of Shabbat.”
“Your foot” (singular) is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: רַגְלוֹ אַחַת בְּתוֹךְ הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's ruling to an even smaller case: just one foot outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One foot outside the תחום counts as being outside, so he may not come back in.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he may come back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא from a ברייתא that rules the opposite: with one foot in and one foot out, he may come back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא taught: If one foot is inside the תחום and one foot is outside, he may come back in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי חנינא with a ברייתא that gives the exact opposite ruling in the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is identical: one foot in and one foot out. The ruling is reversed: he may come back in. A ברייתא is an authoritative source, so רבי חנינא's ruling seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא taught (introduces a contradiction)
A teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: But wasn’t it taught in a baraita:
If one of his feet is within the limit
and his other foot is beyond the limit, he may reenter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי חנינא's ruling in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's ruling that one foot outside forbids coming back in.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules the exact opposite in the identical case.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows אחרים, who go by most of the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows אחרים, who say a person is judged by where most of his body is. רבי חנינא follows a different view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is אחרים. As a ברייתא taught: אחרים say: a person is counted as being in the place where most of his body is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא is not the only opinion; it follows a specific group called אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים say we look at where most of the body is. With one foot out, most of the person is still inside, so he may come back in. רבי חנינא follows the other view, which counts even one foot. So the two sources are simply a disagreement between תנאים, not a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
'Others,' a תנא quoted without his name
Most of him (most of his body)
Counted as being, assigned to

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא: even one foot outside counts. אחרים: we follow where most of the body is. The ברייתא follows אחרים.

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Aḥerim,
as it was taught: Aḥerim say:
He is assigned to the place where most of his body is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be a universal ruling against רבי חנינא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects only the view of אחרים, who go by most of the body. רבי חנינא follows the other view.

steps.title: Second version: one foot inside, he may come back in
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רבי חנינא rules that a person with one foot inside the תחום and one foot outside may come back in. He reads the word in the פסוק as plural, רגליך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רבי חנינא said: if one foot is inside the תחום and one foot is outside, he may come back in. The פסוק says 'If you turn back your foot (רגלך) because of שבת', and we read it as 'your feet' (רגליך).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי חנינא's statement, and here his ruling is the opposite of Step 8. Now he says that a person with one foot outside may come back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 8, רבי חנינא learned from the written form רגלך (one foot) that even one foot outside counts as leaving. In this version he uses the way the word is read, רגליך (feet). On that reading, you only count as 'out' when both feet are out, so one foot out is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: introduces a second version of a statement
We read it as (the spoken reading of the word)
Your feet (plural)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In Step 8, רבי חנינא said he may NOT come back in. In this version he says he MAY come back in. The two versions disagree about what רבי חנינא actually said.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabbi Chanina said:
If one of his feet is inside the Shabbat boundary
and his other foot is outside the boundary
he may come back in,
as it is written: 'If you turn back your foot because of Shabbat'
We read it as 'your feet' (plural).
phrases.notes: Only when both feet are out does he count as having left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of רבי חנינא's ruling from Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One foot inside and one foot outside: he may come back in, because the פסוק is read as 'feet'.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he may not come back in
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second version from a ברייתא that rules he may not come back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: he may not come back in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second version of רבי חנינא with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of Step 9. There the ברייתא said 'may come back in' and challenged the first version. Here a ברייתא says 'may not come back in' and challenges the second version.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא: introduces a challenge from a ברייתא
He may not come back in
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: But it was taught: he may not come back in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's second-version ruling that he may come back in
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules directly against him in the same case.

steps.title: רבי חנינא follows אחרים, who go by the majority of the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי חנינא follows אחרים, who say a person belongs to the place where most of his body is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like אחרים, as a ברייתא teaches: a person is counted by the place where most of his body is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי חנינא is not arguing with every ברייתא; he simply follows the view of אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים judge a person by where most of his body is, and here most of his body is still inside the תחום, so he may come back in. The ברייתא that forbids it follows a different opinion. Notice the flip from Step 10: there, the ברייתא was the one that followed אחרים.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others': a name for a תנא whose view is quoted
The majority of him (most of his body)
Is counted or judged as being in

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the ruling that allows a person with one foot outside to come back in is linked to אחרים, who go by most of the body.

phrases.english: He said it in line with Acherim,
as it was taught: he is counted by the place where most of his body is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the statement to a specific תנא (אחרים) who disagrees with the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי חנינא contradicts an accepted ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא follows אחרים, who go by most of the body. The ברייתא follows a different opinion.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר in the משנה: two אמות yes, three no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's words from the משנה to set up a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: if he went out two אמות, he may come back in. If he went out three, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי אליעזר. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added here. The גמרא simply puts רבי אליעזר's exact words in front of us so that they can be compared with a ברייתא that quotes him differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (אמות)
Three (אמות)
A cubit, a unit of length of about an arm's length

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
two cubits, he may come back in;
three, he may not come back in.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as the opening of the challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר שְׁתַּיִם יִכָּנֵס שָׁלֹשׁ לֹא יִכָּנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבי חנינא and returns to רבי אליעזר in the משנה (Step 7)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: two אמות out, he may come back in; three, he may not.

steps.title: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר as one yes, two no
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר as saying one אמה is allowed but two are not, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר says: one אמה, he may come back in. Two, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's quote of רבי אליעזר with a ברייתא that quotes him with smaller numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, two אמות is allowed. In the ברייתא, two אמות is forbidden. It looks as if the two sources report רבי אליעזר's opinion differently.

keyTerms.meaning: One (אמה)
He may come back in

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
one cubit, he may come back in;
two, he may not come back in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אַחַת — יִכָּנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the quote from Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's report of רבי אליעזר (two allowed, three not)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא reports that two is already forbidden, so the two sources contradict each other about רבי אליעזר's view.

steps.title: Both mean the same thing, counted differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both sources agree; they just count the אמות differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is no difficulty. The משנה means he left the first אמה and is standing in the second. The ברייתא means he left the second אמה and is standing in the third.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no real argument; the משנה and the ברייתא describe the same rule in different words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts the אמה he is standing in, so 'two' means he is standing in the second אמה. The ברייתא counts the אמות he has fully crossed, so 'two' means he crossed two and is standing in the third. Both agree: within the second אמה he may come back in, but once he is in the third he may not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a difficulty
He moved away from (lifted off)
He stands
Two / three (Aramaic)

phrases.english: It is not a difficulty:
This (the Mishna) is where he left the first cubit and stands in the second.
phrases.notes: So he may come back in.

phrases.english: That (the baraita) is where he left the second cubit and stands in the third.
phrases.notes: So he may not come back in.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דַּעֲקַר חֲדָא וְקָם אַתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defines the case: the two sources use different ways of counting the same distance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about how far רבי אליעזר allows.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree: standing in the second אמה, he may come back in; standing in the third, he may not.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: even one אמה is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר as saying that even one אמה outside means he may not come back in.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר says: even one אמה, he may not come back in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge: another ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר as being completely strict.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting the אמות differently cannot fix this one. This ברייתא gives רבי אליעזר no leeway at all, which clashes with the leniency of two אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Even one cubit

phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
even one cubit, he may not come back in!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ אַמָּה אַחַת לֹא יִכָּנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the conclusion of Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's leniency of two אמות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes him as allowing no extra distance at all.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about a person who measured his own 2000 אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the strict ברייתא speaks about a מודד, a person who measured his own exact 2000 אמות. He gets no extra leeway, as a משנה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא speaks about someone who measures his own limit. As a משנה teaches: the person who measures, about whom they said he is given 2000 אמות, even if his measurement ends inside a cave, he may not go further.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the strict ברייתא to a special case, a person who measured out his own 2000 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's leniency of two אמות applies to an ordinary person who stepped out of his תחום. A מודד, who counts out his 2000 אמות himself, gets exactly that measure and nothing more, so even one אמה past it is forbidden. The משנה shows how strict this is: even if his measurement ends in the middle of a cave, he must stop there.

keyTerms.meaning: A person measuring his own limit, for example by counting steps
As we learned in a משנה
2000 cubits, the size of the תחום שבת
The end of his measurement
A cave

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר allows coming back in from up to the second אמה in a regular case. A מודד, who measured his own exact limit, gets no extra room, not even one אמה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the leniency depends on the kind of boundary. A self-measured, exact limit leaves no room for error.

phrases.english: When that baraita was taught, it was about one who measures,
as we learned in a Mishna:
And the one measuring, about whom they said
that he is given two thousand cubits
even if the end of his measurement falls inside a cave.
phrases.notes: Implied: he may not go even one אמה beyond his measured limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the strict ברייתא to a special case (a מודד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר seems to forbid even one אמה in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The strict ruling applies only to a מודד with an exactly measured limit. In a regular case, the leniency of two אמות stands.

steps.title: Even one אמה outside the limit, he may not enter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who is outside the תחום when שבת begins may not enter the town, even if he is only one אמה past the line.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person for whom it became dark outside the תחום may not enter, even if he is only one אמה outside.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. The first opinion, the תנא קמא, gives a strict rule: once שבת starts and you are outside the limit, you cannot come in, even if you are only slightly outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a traveler heading toward a town who is still just past its שבת boundary when night falls. The תנא קמא gives no leeway at all. This is a different case from the previous משנה: there a person walked out of his תחום, and here he was never inside the town's תחום when שבת began.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'
It became dark, meaning Shabbos began
The 2000-אמה Shabbos walking limit
A cubit, roughly an arm's length

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One for whom it grew dark
phrases.notes: Night fell and שבת began while he was traveling.

phrases.english: outside the Shabbos limit
phrases.notes: Outside the 2000 אמות of the town he was heading to.

phrases.english: even one cubit
phrases.notes: Even if he is only a tiny distance outside.

phrases.english: may not enter.
phrases.notes: He must stay where he is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new case: a person caught outside a town's תחום at nightfall, as opposed to the previous משנה's person who went out of his own תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone outside the תחום at nightfall may not enter, even from one אמה away.

steps.title: רבי שמעון allows entry from up to fifteen אמות outside
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees and says the person may enter even from fifteen אמות outside. The reason is that the surveyors deliberately place the marker inside the real limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: even from fifteen אמות outside he may enter. This is because the surveyors do not mark the full measure, on account of people who make mistakes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues with the תנא קמא and gives the person fifteen אמות of leeway. He also explains why he allows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The surveyors who mark the תחום do not put the marker at exactly 2000 אמות. They place it a bit closer to the town, as a safety margin against mistakes. So a person standing up to fifteen אמות past the marker is really still inside the true limit.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who argues and allows entry
Surveyors who measure and mark the תחום
Use up the full measurement, marking right at the very edge
Those who make mistakes

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not allowing a person to step outside the real תחום. His point is that the visible marker sits inside the true 2000 אמות, so this person never actually left the real limit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: He argues with the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: even fifteen cubits
phrases.notes: Even this far past the marker.

phrases.english: he may enter,
phrases.notes: He may walk into the town.

phrases.english: because the surveyors do not mark out the full measures
phrases.notes: They place the marker inside the true 2000 אמות.

phrases.english: because of those who err.
phrases.notes: This leaves a safety margin for mistakes. The גמרא will clarify whose mistakes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמּוֹת יִכָּנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person up to fifteen אמות past the marker may enter, because the marker is set inside the real limit.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains which mistakes the margin guards against
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that 'those who err' means those who make mistakes in the measuring itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: the margin is because of those who err in the measurement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that clarifies one unclear word in רבי שמעון's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'because of those who err' could be understood in different ways. The ברייתא makes it specific: the concern is an error in measuring. Because the surveyors worry that their own measurement might be off, they set the marker a bit inside the 2000 אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא; the discussion of the משנה begins
'It was taught,' introducing a ברייתא
Those who err in measurement

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
phrases.notes: This introduces a ברייתא.

phrases.english: because of those who err in the measurement.
phrases.notes: This defines 'הַטּוֹעִין' in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the reason given by רבי שמעון in Step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הַטּוֹעִין' means those who err in measuring.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק מי שהוציאוהו
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the fourth פרק, מי שהוציאוהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק מי שהוציאוהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The chapter ends here. This is the traditional farewell line said at the end of every פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line adds no new law. It marks the end of the chapter about people whose שבת movement is limited by the תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you,' said when finishing a perek
Name of the perek: 'One who was taken out'

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ends with a dispute. The תנא קמא allows no leeway at all, while רבי שמעון allows fifteen אמות because the marker is set inside the real limit to guard against measuring errors.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Mi Shehotziuhu'
phrases.notes: The closing of the fourth פרק of עירובין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek that ended in Step 21.

steps.title: New פרק: how a city's border is extended
steps.stepSummary: The new perek opens by asking how to 'extend' a city. It begins listing cases where buildings or wall remnants stick in or out of the city's edge.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How does one extend cities? If one house is recessed and one house sticks out, or one turret is recessed and one turret sticks out, or if there were wall remnants ten טפחים high...
steps.whatsHappening: A new perek and a new משנה begin. The משנה asks how we draw a city's border when its edge is uneven, and it starts listing cases. The sentence continues on the next amud, so this step is setting up the rule that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 2000 אמות of the תחום are measured from the city's edge. When the edge is jagged, we draw a straight line across the outermost points, so houses or towers that stick out are included in the city. Wall remnants ten טפחים high also count as part of the city, and the משנה continues with this case next.

keyTerms.meaning: How does one extend, meaning how a city's border is drawn outward
Cities
A turret or tower jutting from a wall
Remnants of walls
Handbreadths

steps.whyThisMatters: Where a city's border lies decides where the 2000-אמה תחום starts. This affects how far every resident may walk on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: How does one extend the cities?
phrases.notes: This opens the new פרק. The title comes from these words.

phrases.english: a house is recessed and a house protrudes,
phrases.notes: The city's edge is uneven because of its houses.

phrases.english: a turret is recessed and a turret protrudes,
phrases.notes: The same idea, applied to towers on the wall.

phrases.english: if there were remnants of walls there
phrases.notes: Leftover pieces of old walls.

phrases.english: ten handbreadths high,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opening statement of a new perek, coming right after the Hadran.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a city's edge is uneven, its border is extended outward to include structures that stick out. The full rule continues on the next amud.
